Where to eat and drink in Totterdown

Updated 2 November 2026. Places open, close and change their hours, so check before you go. Nobody pays to be included. Spotted somewhere missing or closed? Tell us through the contact form. How we check facts.

Totterdown's food and drink is clustered in three places: the Wells Road, which climbs the hill from Three Lamps; Oxford Street, a smaller row of shops near the top; and a handful of corner pubs and cafés on the side streets in between.

Quick answer

  • Brunch: The Sundial Kitchen on William Street, a small vegetarian café; book ahead at weekends. [1] [2]
  • Pizza: Laura's Pizzas (Neapolitan, takeaway and delivery), A Cappella on the Wells Road, or Florence on Oxford Street. [3] [4] [5]
  • Fish and chips: Farrows, 146 Wells Road, a Good Food Award winner in 2020 and 2021. [6] [7]
  • A drink: the Oxford, the Shakespeare, the Star & Dove, the New Found Out and the Thunderbolt; Bruhaha brews its own beer, and Carouse is a wine bar and shop. [4] [8] [9]

What are the best pubs in Totterdown?

Totterdown pubs
PubKnown for
The Oxford, Oxford StreetA locals' favourite for its Sunday roast, plus live music and open mic nights [4] [10] [11]
The Shakespeare, 1 Henry StreetCider, local art on the walls and a walled beer garden [4] [12] [13]
Star & Dove, St Luke's RoadFood and live sport, under new management [4] [14] [15]
The New Found Out, 60 Green StreetLive sport; reopened in October 2021 after a refurbishment [4] [16]
The Thunderbolt, 124 Bath RoadLive music in a Grade II listed former tollhouse [4] [17]

Is the Thunderbolt closing? The freehold has been put up for sale after 18 years under the same landlord, but Bristol24/7 reported it would keep trading and hosting live events until a sale completes. [18]

Where can you get local beer, wine or a cocktail?

  • Bruhaha, 156–158 Wells Road: a brewpub that started as a home brewery in 2019 and opened here in October 2023. [8] Its beers include Three Lamps, an IPA, TotterDowner, a bitter, and Rusty Robot, a porter. [19]
  • Carouse, 32 Oxford Street: a wine shop and bar with more than 200 wines and simple food, opened in 2025 in the former Little Kitchen Cookery School. [9] [20]
  • BANK, 107 Wells Road: coffee by day, cocktails and craft beer by night. [21] [22]
  • Smokebox, 172 Wells Road: smoked barbecue with cocktails, in the former Southside Bar & Kitchen. [23] [24]

Food and drink in Totterdown, street by street

  • Wells Road: BANK (107), Totterdown Canteen (141), Farrows (146), Al Waha (147), Truffled of Totterdown (152), Bruhaha (156–158), Fox & West and Smokebox (172) and A Cappella (184C).
  • Oxford Street: the Oxford, Florence, Carouse (32), Asia Garden (29) and The Bakehouse (118).
  • Side streets: the Sundial Kitchen and Laura's Pizzas (1 William Street), the Shakespeare (1 Henry Street), the New Found Out (60 Green Street) and the Star & Dove (St Luke's Road).
  • Bath Road: the Thunderbolt (124).

Addresses are from the sources in each table above.

Where can you eat with children in Totterdown?

  • Tots & Teapots, Wells Road: a play café with sessions for young children, food and party bookings. [35]
  • Windmill Hill City Farm: a short walk away, with a café open every day and free entry to the farm. [36] [37] See parks and green spaces.

Where to eat during the Totterdown Arts Trail

Many local venues open specially or run pop-ups during the arts trail weekend, which is on 14 and 15 November in 2026. The organisers publish a food and drink list on their website, and the printed trail map is available in local businesses. [30] [38]
